mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters when this trigger is met, or the average rank IC over triggered periods is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60d returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when wage growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the mechanism fails when oil prices are falling sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (change < ±0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of rapidly rising wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS) and S&P 500 5-day returns: higher household savings imply greater future consumption or investment, which supports corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive short-term returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS changes and S&P 500 5d returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests, or the relationship inverts during periods of high uncertainty.
